questions.q: Why does the summary call repeated rereading an ineffective study method?
a: It creates a false sense of mastery that fades quickly
It takes far longer than any other study technique
It works only for people with unusually strong memories
It prevents you from ever feeling familiar with the material
questions.why: Lesson 1 says repetition makes you feel fluent but leaves you unable to recall the basics soon after.

a: Closing the book and actively recalling what you remember
Reading the same chapter several times in a row
Highlighting the most important sentences as you read
Copying key passages into a notebook word for word
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes asking yourself what you remember after closing the book, which activates your memory.

questions.q: What does the summary suggest doing after studying something for a while?
a: Take a short break so your brain can consolidate it
Switch immediately to a completely unrelated subject
Repeat it without pausing until it feels automatic
Test yourself before allowing any rest at all
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends a ten-minute break before repeating material so the brain consolidates it.

questions.q: How can you tell that you truly understand a topic?
a: You can explain it simply enough for a young child to follow
You can recite the textbook definition without looking
You can finish the material faster than your classmates
You can remember it for a few days after an exam
questions.why: Lesson 3 says if you cannot explain a topic simply, you do not fully understand it yet.

questions.q: What does the summary say about linking new information to memories you already have?
a: It expands what you can learn, with no clear limit
It works only for facts you learned as a child
It makes learning slower but more accurate
It should be avoided because it causes confusion
questions.why: Lesson 3 reports that associating new material with older memories has no apparent limit.
